result: EPCAM marks the pancreatic epithelial fraction enriched in PDX1+NKX6-1+ pancreatic progenitors in human fetal pancreas at 7-12 weeks of development. The CD45-CD31-EPCAM+ fraction contains pancreatic progenitor markers while the EPCAM- fraction represents mesenchymal cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 raises a critical concern about 45% of EPCAM+ cells having low PDX1/NKX6-1 levels (Figure 1E), questioning what these cells represent and how they relate to earlier progenitors. The reviewer requests integration of this observation with the authors' previous work, indicating the characterization is incomplete. While the basic EPCAM+ enrichment is not disputed, the heterogeneity within this population requires clarification.

result: GP2 marks a multipotent progenitor population at 7WD that differentiates into acinar (GP2hi), ductal, and endocrine (GP2-) lineages. The temporal dynamics show GP2+ cells (96% at 7WD) giving rise to GP2- (increasing to 34% by 8.4WD), GP2hi (appearing at 9.4WD, reaching 20% by 12WD), and Elow populations (appearing at 8.6WD, reaching 18% by 12WD).
evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes the novelty is decreased by the authors' recent Cell Reports 2017 paper characterizing GP2 as a progenitor marker. More critically, the reviewers request clarification on whether GP2+ represents truly multipotent cells or a mixture of lineage-committed progenitors (Reviewer 2 asks about PTF1a, Cpa1, c-Myc expression). The temporal data is accepted but the interpretation of multipotency requires additional evidence.

result: Development toward the acinar lineage is marked by increased GP2 expression, with the GP2hi population showing enrichment of acinar markers (CEL, CELA3A, CTRC) and 85% of GP2hi-enriched genes being preferentially expressed in adult acinar cells.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the acinar differentiation findings. The data showing acinar marker enrichment in GP2hi cells and correlation with adult acinar gene expression is accepted without critique.

result: Endocrine differentiation involves downregulation of GP2 and CD142 with upregulation of NEUROG3. NEUROG3 first appears in the GP2-CD142- population at 8.4WD before the Elow population emerges, then becomes enriched in the ElowCD142-SUSD2+ subset from 8.6WD onward.
evaluation: The temporal sequence of NEUROG3 expression and its enrichment in specific populations is well-documented with RT-qPCR data. Reviewers do not challenge these findings, though Reviewer 3 requests additional analysis of other endocrine cell types beyond beta cells.

result: Endocrine maturation progresses through sequential marker changes: CD142 downregulation, SUSD2 upregulation, and ECAD level decrease. The GP2-CD142+SUSD2- subset (95% at 7WD) transitions to CD142-SUSD2- (increasing to 43% by 11.3WD), then to CD142-SUSD2+ in the Elow population (48% at 8.6WD, decreasing to 10% by 12WD).
evaluation: The temporal flow cytometry data showing sequential marker expression changes is well-documented and not challenged by reviewers. The progression model is accepted as describing endocrine maturation stages.

result: At 8.6WD, endocrine markers (CHGA, NEUROD1, NKX2-2, INS) are exclusively in the ElowCD142-SUSD2+ subset. By 10-12WD, INS becomes exclusive to the ElowCD142-SUSD2- subset. Single-cell analysis shows the GP2-CD142-SUSD2- subset is heterogeneous (78% CFTR+, 16% NEUROG3+) while ElowCD142-SUSD2+ is enriched for NEUROG3+ cells (74%) co-expressing NEUROD1 and NKX2-2.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 raises a critical question about whether two distinct beta cell populations have been identified based on the temporal shift in INS expression between SUSD2+ and SUSD2- subsets. This interpretation requires clarification. Reviewer 3 also requests analysis of other hormone-expressing cells (GCG, polyhormonal cells) and their distribution in these populations, which is not provided.

result: Transcriptomic analysis shows GP2hi and GP2+ populations are enriched for digestion-related processes, while the Elow population is enriched for endocrine functions (insulin/peptide secretion, hormone secretion). The Elow population contains 91-34 differentially expressed genes (98-100% enriched in adult endocrine cells) including endocrine transcription factors (ARX, PAX4, PAX6, NEUROD1, MAFA, MAFB, ISL1, NKX2.2) and hormones (CHGA, GCG, GHRL, INS).
evaluation: Reviewers request substantial improvements to computational analyses: (1) unclear cut-offs for defining enriched genes, (2) genes underlying GO terms should be listed in supplementary tables, (3) correlation methods with single-cell RNAseq not described, (4) heatmaps show limited genes without justification for selection (Reviewer 1). Reviewer 2 requests inclusion of additional datasets (Muraro et al. 2016) and all endocrine cell types (not just alpha/beta). Reviewer 1 specifically asks about PAX4 expression timing and cell-type specificity.

result: In vitro hPSC-derived pancreatic endocrine cells recapitulate in vivo developmental stages, showing similar CD142/ECAD/SUSD2 expression patterns and temporal dynamics as human fetal pancreas. The ECADlowCD142-SUSD2+ population in hPSC-derived cells expresses NEUROG3, NEUROD1, and NKX2-2 similar to 8.6WD fetal pancreas.
evaluation: Reviewer 4 requests clarification on which of the 3 hPSC lines were used for which experiments and whether results are comparable across lines. The side-by-side comparison is noted as valuable but the experimental details are insufficient. Reviewers also note that hPSC-derived cells display fetal rather than adult phenotypes, which limits the interpretation of full developmental recapitulation.

result: The GP2- population expresses both ductal markers (CFTR, KRT19, SPP1) and endocrine progenitor markers (NEUROG3), suggesting it contains multiple cell types including ductal and endocrine progenitors.
evaluation: The heterogeneity of the GP2- population is supported by marker expression data and is consistent with the single-cell analysis showing mixed populations. Reviewers do not challenge this interpretation.

result: GP2 and ECAD expression segregate the EPCAM+ fraction into four distinct populations (GP2hi, GP2+, GP2-, Elow) at 9.4WD with consistent frequencies across individuals, demonstrating inter-individual homogeneity.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 requests presentation of GP2/ECAD staining for all populations shown in Figure 2A (not just the blue square), indicating incomplete data presentation. Reviewer 3 requests more quantitative summaries and statistical comparisons across all experiments rather than single representative plots.

result: Human fetal pancreases were obtained from 7-13 weeks of development with appropriate ethical approval and maternal consent. Ages were determined by last menstrual period and morphology.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 questions the precision of developmental timing (e.g., '7.4 WD') and requests clarification on whether replicates are biological or technical. Reviewer 1 suggests a supplementary table detailing all human tissue samples used. Reviewer 3 notes methods are only superficially described with no detailed supplementary methods.
